rationale: The Olden/power benchmark is a pointer-chasing, tree-traversal-driven simulation whose hot paths are recursive linked-data-structure walks, so cost tolerance on those dimensions signals where each pass may apply: SUB and SPLIT are nearly free instruction- and block-level transforms with negligible correctness exposure, so they receive high weights across all dimensions and will saturate coverage; FLA is the strongest control-flow-hiding pass and suits power's branchy traversal code, but it adds dispatch-loop overhead and carries moderate risk around irreducible/exception-style control, so it is favored on security/diversity with only moderate runtime tolerance; BCF and IBR both inflate hot-path work (bogus basic blocks and indirect branching penalize tight pointer-chasing loops) and are kept at low runtime/size tolerance so the selector applies them only to functions whose features justify it; ICALL gets the lowest runtime and correctness tolerance because power is call-intensive and added indirect-call dispatch on recursion-heavy paths risks both measurable slowdown and devirtualization-sensitive miscompiles; IGV sits at neutral 0.5s since the profile is empty (no static feature data), letting function-level features decide rather than biasing the pass up front. Overall the table biases toward cheap high-coverage transforms (SUB, SPLIT, FLA) while gating the expensive dynamic-obfuscation passes (BCF, IBR, ICALL) behind strong supporting features, preserving correctness and keeping aggregate runtime/size overhead acceptable.
